text: If you switched jobs this year, your old employer's 401k is still yours and you have several options — you can leave it, roll it to your new employer's plan, or roll it to an IRA. The IRA rollover almost always gives you the most investment options and the lowest fees. The one time to skip it: if your new employer plan has institutional funds you can't access otherwise.
label: information

text: A thing a lot of people miss: you can make an IRA contribution for the previous tax year up until the April filing deadline, not just until December 31. If you haven't maxed 2024 yet and you have the money, you still can.
label: information

text: The debt avalanche pays less interest than the debt snowball over time, but research consistently shows people complete it less often. The snowball is worth the extra interest if you're someone who needs the psychological win of a zero balance to stay on track. Know which one you are before you pick a method.
label: information

text: HSAs are the only triple-tax-advantaged account: contributions are pre-tax, growth is tax-free, and withdrawals for medical expenses are tax-free. After age 65 you can withdraw for anything penalty-free, just paying income tax like a traditional IRA. The play most people miss: invest the HSA, pay medical bills out of pocket, and keep the receipts forever — you can reimburse yourself years later.
label: information

text: Your credit score is not a measure of wealth. It measures how reliably you borrow and repay. Someone with $0 in savings but a long history of on-time payments can have a higher score than someone with $200,000 in investments who only uses cash. text: My credit score crossed 800 for the first time today. Six years ago it was below 600.
label: milestone

text: The 'latte factor' advice that cutting coffee will make you rich is wrong, but the underlying idea — that small recurring expenses compound over time — is correct. The issue is that coffee is not most people's actual leak. Subscriptions, unused memberships, and restaurant spending usually are.
label: information

text: If your employer offers an FSA (flexible spending account), the annual contribution limit for 2024 is $3,200. This money is pre-tax, which means you save your marginal rate on every dollar. The catch is it's use-it-or-lose-it each year, so only contribute what you'll realistically spend on qualified medical, dental, and vision expenses.
label: information

text: Carrying a small credit card balance to 'build credit' is a myth. Your credit score does not benefit from paying interest. What matters is utilizing the card and paying the statement balance in full and on time. The 'keep a small balance' advice costs you money and does nothing for your score.
label: information

text: When comparing job offers, don't forget to value the 401k match as part of your compensation. A job offering $80k with a 4% match on $80k provides $3,200 per year in match — meaning the total comp is $83,200 before benefits. A job at $85k with no match might actually pay less in year one.
label: information

text: The 4% rule for retirement withdrawal comes from the Trinity Study and was designed for 30-year retirement periods. If you plan to retire at 50, you should use a lower withdrawal rate — 3% or 3.5% is more commonly cited for longer horizons. The 4% rule is not a law; it's a guideline calibrated to specific assumptions.
label: information

text: I-bonds can only be purchased directly from TreasuryDirect.gov, not through brokerage accounts. The annual purchase limit is $10,000 per person electronically, plus $5,000 with a tax refund. You can't cash them in the first year, and there's a 3-month interest penalty if you cash before 5 years.
label: information

text: Medical debt collections have special rules other debt doesn't. As of 2023, medical debt under $500 can no longer be reported to the major credit bureaus. For debt over $500, it can't appear until at least a year after going to collections. This doesn't mean you don't owe it — it just means the credit impact is more limited.
label: information

text: When you get a raise, your entire income is not taxed at the new higher rate. The US uses a marginal tax system: only the dollars within each bracket are taxed at that rate. If you move from the 22% to the 24% bracket, only the income above the 22% bracket ceiling gets taxed at 24%.
label: information

text: Series EE savings bonds purchased today are guaranteed to double in value in 20 years, regardless of the stated interest rate. That's an effective guaranteed return of 3.5% annualized. This makes them worth comparing to CDs or long-term bond funds for the 20-year portion of your savings, not the short-term portion.
label: information

text: A Roth IRA has a contribution limit, but it does not have a limit on conversions. If you have money in a traditional IRA, you can convert any amount to a Roth in a given year — you'll owe income tax on the converted amount, but there's no cap. This is how the backdoor Roth works for high earners.
label: information

text: The best time to negotiate a salary is at the point of job offer, not during a performance review. At the offer stage you have maximum leverage because the employer has already decided they want you and switching costs are highest. During a review, raises are often budgeted and constrained before the conversation begins.
label: information

text: If you receive a penalty notice from the IRS, read it carefully before assuming you owe it. The IRS sends a significant number of incorrect notices, particularly for under-reported income, that result from mismatched 1099s or data entry errors. You can respond by mail with documentation; you do not have to pay a disputed amount immediately.
label: information

text: Target-date retirement funds are a reasonable default for most people. They automatically shift from stocks to bonds as you approach retirement and rebalance automatically. The main thing to check is the expense ratio — anything below 0.20% is good, anything above 0.50% is worth questioning.
label: information

text: The difference between a debit card and a credit card in terms of fraud protection is significant. Debit card disputes require you to prove the charge was fraudulent; credit card disputes reverse the charge immediately while the investigation runs. For this reason alone, using a credit card for day-to-day purchases and paying it off monthly is worth it for most people.
label: information

text: Your credit report and your credit score are two different things. You're entitled to free reports from all three bureaus at AnnualCreditReport.com — these show the underlying data. Your score is a number derived from that data by a scoring model. Checking your score does not require checking all three reports, and vice versa.
label: information

text: Employer matches in a 401k are sometimes subject to a vesting schedule. This means the matched money isn't fully yours until you've worked there for a certain number of years. Before leaving a job, check your vesting status — leaving six months early has cost people thousands in unvested match.
label: information

text: Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is typically required when you put less than 20% down on a conventional loan. The cost is usually 0.5%–1.5% of the loan amount per year. It drops off automatically when you reach 20% equity based on the original purchase price, or you can request removal when you hit 20% based on current value with an appraisal.
label: information

text: If you have high-interest credit card debt, a balance transfer card with a 0% promotional period can save you a significant amount in interest — but there are real catches. Most charge a 3%–5% transfer fee upfront. The 0% rate is temporary, often 12–21 months. And if you miss a payment, some issuers void the promotion immediately.
label: information

text: You can deduct student loan interest on your federal taxes if your income is under about $85,000 single or $170,000 married. The maximum deduction is $2,500. You don't need to itemize — it's an 'above the line' deduction that reduces your AGI directly.
label: information

text: When you roll over a 401k, request a direct rollover to the new institution rather than taking the check yourself. If the check is made out to you, the plan administrator is required to withhold 20% for taxes — even if you intend to roll it over. You'd then have to make up that 20% out of pocket within 60 days to avoid it being treated as a distribution.
label: information

text: Life insurance is not an investment. Whole life and universal life policies that include an investment component almost always return less than buying term insurance and investing the premium difference in index funds. The people who benefit most from whole life are usually the ones selling it.
label: information

text: If your adjusted gross income is under about $36,000 single (or $72,000 married), you may qualify for the Saver's Credit, which is a tax credit of up to 50% of your IRA or 401k contributions up to $2,000. Unlike a deduction, this directly reduces your tax bill. A lot of early-career savers miss it.
label: information

text: Crypto is treated as property by the IRS, not currency. Every time you sell crypto, trade one crypto for another, or use crypto to buy something, you've triggered a taxable event. The gain or loss is calculated based on your cost basis (what you paid). Forgetting this is a very common way people underreport income.
label: information

text: The annual gift tax exclusion for 2024 is $18,000 per person, per recipient. You can give up to this amount to any number of people without filing a gift tax return. Above that threshold, you need to file Form 709, but you likely won't owe tax until your lifetime total gifts exceed the federal estate tax exemption.
label: information

text: Most employer health plans have an open enrollment window, usually in the fall, where you can make changes. Outside of open enrollment, changes are only allowed after a qualifying life event: marriage, divorce, birth, adoption, or loss of other coverage. Missing open enrollment usually means you're locked in for another year.
label: information

text: FDIC insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per institution, per account category. If you have both a savings and a checking account at the same bank, they're in the same category and share the $250k limit — not $500k total. To insure more, spread money across institutions or use different account categories (individual vs. joint).
label: information

text: When comparing a HDHP with HSA to a traditional PPO, the math usually favors the HDHP if you're healthy and don't expect significant medical expenses. The HSA contributions reduce your taxable income and can be invested. The PPO wins if you have ongoing prescriptions or planned procedures that the PPO covers better.
label: information

text: The penalty for early withdrawal from a traditional IRA or 401k is 10% of the withdrawn amount on top of ordinary income taxes. But there are exceptions: certain medical expenses, first-home purchase (IRA only, up to $10,000), disability, substantially equal periodic payments, and others. The list is specific and worth checking before assuming you can't access the money.
label: information

text: 529 plans have no income limit — anyone can open and contribute regardless of earnings. Contributions are made with after-tax dollars at the federal level, but 34 states offer a state income tax deduction for contributions. You can contribute to any state's 529 regardless of where you or the beneficiary live.
label: information

text: Negotiating medical bills is usually possible and often successful, especially if you're paying cash. Hospitals typically charge insurers a fraction of the listed rate, and they'll often offer uninsured patients similar discounts if asked. Call the billing department, explain your situation, and ask what the cash-pay rate is. The worst answer is no.
label: information

text: Dollar-cost averaging — investing a fixed amount at regular intervals regardless of market conditions — doesn't outperform lump-sum investing on average. Studies consistently show lump-sum beats DCA about two-thirds of the time. DCA's value is psychological: it reduces the anxiety of 'what if I invest right before a crash,' which for most people is worth the slight expected return cost.
label: information

text: If you're self-employed and you contribute to a SEP-IRA, you can contribute up to 25% of net self-employment income, up to $69,000 for 2024. The contribution is deductible and reduces your taxable income. You have until the tax filing deadline (including extensions) to make the contribution for the prior year.
label: information

text: When you receive an inheritance, the assets usually receive a 'stepped-up' cost basis to the fair market value at the date of death. This means if your parent bought stock for $10,000 that's worth $100,000 when they die, and you sell it immediately, your taxable gain is $0, not $90,000.
label: information

text: The order of operations for where to put money most personal finance guides recommend: 1) contribute enough to get any employer match, 2) build a 3-6 month emergency fund, 3) pay off high-interest debt, 4) max a Roth or traditional IRA, 5) max the 401k, 6) invest in a taxable brokerage account. Most people skip steps and jump to 6 before doing 1.
label: information

text: Social Security benefits are reduced if you claim before full retirement age (67 for people born after 1960) and increased if you delay past it, up to age 70. Claiming at 62 gives you about 70% of your full benefit; waiting until 70 gives you about 124%. The breakeven point where waiting pays off is usually somewhere in your mid-80s.
label: information

text: A W-4 is not a fixed document. You can update it at any time by submitting a new form to your employer's HR department. If you have a life change — marriage, divorce, a child, a second job — it's worth revisiting to make sure your withholding is still accurate. The IRS withholding estimator at irs.gov is the most reliable way to check.
label: information

text: In most states, a spouse is not legally responsible for the other spouse's student loan debt incurred before marriage. The exception is if you live in a community property state and the loans were taken on during the marriage. Prenuptial agreements can also change this. Worth knowing before assuming debt is shared.
label: information

text: When refinancing a mortgage, 'no closing cost' refinancing is not free. The costs are rolled into either a higher interest rate or added to the loan balance. The right choice depends on how long you plan to stay in the home. If you'll move in two years, a no-cost refi can make sense. If you're staying 10 years, paying closing costs upfront almost always wins.
label: information

text: The mental accounting mistake: treating money differently based on where it came from. A tax refund is not a windfall — it's your own money the government held for you interest-free. A bonus is not free money — it's part of your compensation. Treating either as special tends to lead to spending you wouldn't do with regular paycheck money.
label: information

text: If you have more than 20% equity in your home, you can request to have PMI removed without waiting for automatic cancellation. Contact your lender and ask about their appraisal requirements. In a market where home values have increased significantly, you may already be at 20% equity based on current value even if you're not based on original purchase price.
label: information

text: Fees in index funds matter because they compound the same way returns do — but in reverse. A fund with a 0.03% expense ratio versus one with a 0.75% expense ratio doesn't sound like much. Over 30 years on a $100,000 investment returning 7% annually, the difference is roughly $48,000 in additional wealth.
label: information

text: The annual contribution limit for 401k accounts in 2024 is $23,000 for employees, plus a $7,500 catch-up contribution if you're 50 or older. The employer match does not count toward this limit — the total limit including employer contributions is $69,000.
label: information

text: If you're in a low income year — just graduated, took a career break, changed jobs — it's often an ideal time to do a Roth conversion. You'll pay taxes on the converted amount at your current lower rate, and those dollars grow tax-free going forward. A tax professional can calculate how much to convert to fill your current bracket without jumping to the next one.
label: information

text: Most states have unclaimed property registries where companies that can't find you send money you're owed — old bank accounts, utility deposits, forgotten paychecks. You can search your state's registry for free at most states' treasurer websites. About 1 in 10 Americans has unclaimed property. It takes about 10 minutes to check.
label: information

text: When calculating whether to pay off debt or invest, the comparison isn't just the interest rate vs. expected market return. Factor in: is the debt interest deductible? Is there an employer match available that represents an instant 50-100% return? Are you comparing to tax-advantaged or taxable investment returns? The simple interest rate comparison misses a lot.
label: information

text: I have $3,000 in savings and $9,500 in credit card debt at 23% APR. I know I should pay the card but every time I look at my savings balance going down it makes me anxious. Is there a way to handle both at the same time or do I just have to get over the feeling and throw everything at the debt?
label: advice_seeking
